{"body":"## Summary

Rich, range-styled text for Pathland: an **`AttributedString`** model, inline-**Markdown** parsing, transmitted as a structured arena payload via a new **`STYLE::SET_ATTRIBUTED_TEXT`** command, and rendered natively on every surface (GTK/pango, SSR HTML, DOM client).

The 16-byte opcode is untouched — all variable-length data (text + runs) lives in the **arena** as one length-prefixed entry, referenced by offset. This mirrors how `SET_TEXT` works today.

## Design

### Wire: `STYLE::SET_ATTRIBUTED_TEXT` (0x04)

`A=nodeId, B=arenaRef (payload), C=0`.

Arena payload (one `[u32 byteLength][bytes]` entry):

```
[ u32 textLen ][ utf8 text ]
[ u32 styleRunCount ][ style runs... ]
[ u32 linkCount ][ links... ]
```

- **Tagged style run**: `(u32 start)(u32 end)(u8 count) ((u16 propId)(4-byte value)) × count` — reuses the existing text-format property vocabulary (`FONT_SIZE` 0x1007, `FONT_WEIGHT` 0x1008, `FONT_STYLE` 0x1017, `FONT_DESIGN` 0x1018, `COLOR` 0x100A, `UNDERLINE`, `STRIKETHROUGH`, …); values use the standard encodings (F32/enum LE, packed ARGB, U8). Node-level properties remain the base; runs override ranges.
- **Link**: `(u32 start)(u32 end)(u8 urlLen)(utf8 url)` — links are a separate section so style runs stay 4-byte-valued only.

### Shared Markdown parser (one parser for every DSL)

New `no_std` + `alloc` crate **`pathland-markdown`**: parses an inline subset —

- `**bold**`, `*italic*`, `` `code` ``, `~~strikethrough~~`, `[link](url)`

— into the AttributedString/payload. Used natively by the Rust DSL; exported as a **cdylib C ABI** and bound by Java via **JNA** (embedded in a shim jar, the `pathland-render-html` pattern) so `Markdown.parse(...)` shares the exact same parser across all DSLs. (Consequence: Java markdown parsing adds a native dependency; the `AttributedString` *builder* stays pure Java.)

### DSL surface

- **Java**: `AttributedString` builder (range-tracking fluent builder), `Text.of(AttributedString)`, `Markdown.parse(String)` (JNA).
- **Rust** (`pathland-view`): the same builder + parser, natively.
- **Fine-grained**: `Text.of(Signal<AttributedString>)` re-emits `SET_ATTRIBUTED_TEXT` only when the encoded payload changes (zero opcodes when unchanged).

### Renderers

- **GTK4** (`pathland-render-gtk`): build one `pango::AttrList` from the runs — `AttrWeight`, `AttrStyle`, `AttrSize`, `AttrForeground`, … plus **`PANGO_ATTR_LINK`** for link runs — set on the `GtkLabel`.
- **SSR HTML** (`pathland-render-html`): emit the text as nested styled `<span>` runs (reusing the existing inline-style mapping) and `<a href>` for links.
- **DOM client** (`@pathland/dom-renderer`): hydrate the SSR spans; apply deltas surgically with **`document.createRange()` + `splitText`/`surroundContents`** (wrap only the changed character range in a styled span; full rebuild only for wholesale payload changes). `Range` is browser-only — SSR still emits spans.

### Conformance

Golden byte vectors for `SET_ATTRIBUTED_TEXT` and the arena payload (`spec/CONFORMANCE.md`); cross-renderer mapping tests; per-project `status.md` updates.

## Phases

1. **Protocol + core**: `spec/OPCODE.md` (command + arena payload), `spec/MODIFIERS.md`/`spec/PRIMITIVES.md` (text/attribute notes), `pathland-core` encode/decode, `CONFORMANCE.md` vectors.
2. **Shared parser**: `pathland-markdown` crate + cdylib C ABI + Java JNA shim.
3. **DSLs**: Rust + Java `AttributedString` builders, `Text.of(AttributedString)`, `Markdown.parse`, signal bindings.
4. **Renderers**: GTK pango, SSR HTML spans, DOM client `createRange` deltas.
5. **Tests + status.md** across all implementing projects.

## Constraints

- Protocol-first: spec + conformance vectors before implementation.
- Fixed 16-byte opcodes (the payload is arena-only).
- `no_std` core; zero dynamic allocation in steady-state emission.
- Stateless renderers: the run tree is a pure function of the opcode stream.

---

## Command Tables

### TREE (0x01)

The `componentType` values (the primitive views the protocol supports) are
catalogued in [PRIMITIVES.md](./PRIMITIVES.md), grouped by their SwiftUI
counterpart. Component IDs are allocated there spec-first; this file remains
the wire-format authority.

| Command | Value | A | B | C | Flags | Description |
|---------|-------|---|---|---|-------|-------------|
| `CREATE_NODE` | `0x01` | nodeId | componentType (u16, low) | 0 | — | Create a node of `componentType` |
| `DELETE_NODE` | `0x02` | nodeId | 0 | 0 | — | Delete a node and its subtree |
| `INSERT_CHILD` | `0x03` | parentId | childId | index | — | Insert `childId` into `parentId` at `index`; append is `index = u32::MAX` (`APPEND`) |
| `REMOVE_CHILD` | `0x04` | parentId | childId | 0 | — | Remove `childId` from `parentId` |
| `MOVE_CHILD` | `0x05` | parentId | childId | newIndex | — | Move child to `newIndex` (after removal); append is `newIndex = u32::MAX` (`APPEND`) |

### PARAMETER (0x02)

The engine does not emit positions. `PARAMETER` carries the **constraint properties**
that native renderers feed to their own layout — spacing, alignment, FILL/HUG
size hints — plus **styling modifiers** (padding, colors, fonts, borders).

| Command | Value | A | B | C | Flags | Description |
|---------|-------|---|---|---|-------|-------------|
| `SET_PROPERTY` | `0x01` | nodeId | propertyId (u16, low) + valueType (u8, high byte) | value | — | Set a constraint/style property; `value` depends on `valueType` |
| `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` | `0x02` | arenaRef (path) | valueType (u8) | value | — | Override a design token; path is an arena string |
| `SET_TEXT` | `0x03` | nodeId | arenaRef (utf8) | 0 | — | Set a node's text content |
| `SET_DATE` | `0x04` | nodeId | days since epoch (I32) | millis of day (U32) | — | Set a node's date value (e.g. a `DATE_PICKER`); see [EVENTS.md](./EVENTS.md#date) for the matching `DATE_CHANGED` event |

`SET_PROPERTY` encodes the value type in the **high byte of `B`** (bits 24–31) and the property id in the low two bytes:

```
B = (valueType << 16) | propertyId
```

#### Value types

| Value Type | Value | C / value encoding |
|------------|-------|--------------------|
| `U8` | `0x01` | low byte of C |
| `U32` | `0x02` | u32 |
| `I32` | `0x03` | i32 |
| `F32` | `0x04` | f32 |
| `STRING` | `0x05` | arenaRef (utf8) |
| `ENUM` | `0x06` | low byte of C |
| `COLOR` | `0x07` | packed `0xAARRGGBB` |
| `DESIGN_TOKEN` | `0x08` | arenaRef (token path) |
| `LIST` | `0x09` | arenaRef (length-prefixed array, see below) |

> **Enum-valued properties** (`ALIGNMENT`, `TEXT_ALIGNMENT`, `TRUNCATION_MODE`,
> `ROLE`, `STATE`, and the draft `FONT_*`/`CONTENT_MODE`/`CONTROL_SIZE`/`SHAPE_KIND`
> properties) are carried with the **`F32` value type**, holding the numeric enum
> code as an f32 bit pattern (e.g. `ALIGNMENT=Center(1)` → `C = 1.0f32.to_bits()`).
> The enumerated code tables live in
> [MODIFIERS.md](./MODIFIERS.md#appendix-enumerated-values). The `ENUM` value type
> (low byte of `C`) is available for explicitly `ENUM`-coded properties.
>
> **Token references**: any property that normally carries a `COLOR` / `F32` /
> `STRING` / `ENUM` value MAY instead carry the `DESIGN_TOKEN` value type, with
> `C` = arenaRef to a token path (see [Design Token System](#design-token-system)
> and [TOKENS.md](./TOKENS.md)).
>
> **`LIST` arrays**: a `LIST` value (`C` = arenaRef) is a length-prefixed array in
> the string arena: `[u32 count][element × count]`, each element a `u32` holding
> the value-type's bit pattern — currently produced with each element a `F32`
> (the `FIT_QUERY` threshold table), so `bytes = 4 + 4·count`. The count is the
> first `u32` (little-endian); a zero count is an empty list. Decoders read the
> element count, never infer it from the arena length, so a property can re-emit
> a shorter list with the arena entry intact.

#### Constraint properties for native layout

The following properties drive native layout; the renderer maps them to its
native layout properties (e.g. `SPACING` → a gap between children,
`WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` → size requests). Special `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` values: `-1` = FILL
(expand to available), `-2` = HUG_CONTENT (native intrinsic size).

> **Allocation semantics** — the exact meaning of a Fixed / `FILL` / `HUG_CONTENT`
> size, how containers distribute space to children (main axis: only `FILL`
> expands; cross axis: children hug unless `FILL`), and how content fits inside
> a Fixed box, are defined in [LAYOUT.md](./LAYOUT.md).

> **Units — logical points.** All size properties (`WIDTH`/`HEIGHT`/`SPACING`/
> `PADDING`/`CONTENT_MARGINS`, …) are expressed in an abstract **logical point**
> unit — the same abstraction as SwiftUI points, Jetpack Compose `dp`, and CSS
> pixels. A renderer MUST allocate the requested points box and fit content
> within it; it must never treat the value as a device-pixel size. Each renderer
> maps points to its native unit and resolves its own device resolution (logical
> points × scale factor), so the same value yields the same physical size across
> renderers.

| Property | Value | Type | Native meaning |
|----------|-------|------|----------------|
| `SPACING` | `0x0001` | F32 | Gap between children |
| `ALIGNMENT` | `0x0002` | F32 (enum code) | Cross-axis position (never stretches; default = Leading, `Fill`(3) = default hug — see LAYOUT.md) |
| `CONTENT_MARGINS` | `0x0005` | F32 | Uniform inset between a stack's edge and its content |
| `WIDTH` | `0x100B` | F32 | Width hint (-1 FILL, -2 HUG) |
| `HEIGHT` | `0x100C` | F32 | Height hint (-1 FILL, -2 HUG) |
| `GRID_COLUMNS` | `0x001E` | F32 | Grid column count (positive = count, -1/absent = auto-fit; a count, never a pixel width — see PRIMITIVES.md §Grid) |
| `GRID_ROWS` | `0x001F` | F32 | Grid row count (positive = count, -1/absent = auto-fit) |
| `GRID_TRACKS` | `0x0020` | STRING | Per-track grid spec (`flex`/`fixed:<pts>`/`adaptive:<pts>`, comma-separated) — takes precedence over the counts |

#### Text properties

Text-bearing nodes (`TEXT`, `BUTTON` labels, `TEXT_FIELD`) carry their content
via `SET_TEXT` (0x03) and their layout via these properties:

| Property | Value | Type | Native meaning |
|----------|-------|------|----------------|
| `TEXT` | `0x000A` | STRING | The text content (a `SET_TEXT`-style arena string) |
| `LINE_LIMIT` | `0x000B` | U32 | Maximum number of lines (0 = unlimited) |
| `TEXT_ALIGNMENT` | `0x000C` | F32 (enum code) | Alignment of the text block within its bounds |
| `TRUNCATION_MODE` | `0x000D` | F32 (enum code) | Truncation style when text overflows (`Head`/`Middle`/`Tail`) |

Enumerated values for these and every other enum-valued property are
consolidated in [MODIFIERS.md](./MODIFIERS.md#appendix-enumerated-values).

#### Styling properties (modifiers)

Styling properties are **modifiers** — they apply to any view, not just stacks —
and map to visual decoration rather than layout. `PADDING` (uniform) and its
per-edge variants map to native padding, alongside
`COLOR`/`BACKGROUND_COLOR`/`BORDER_*`:

| Property | Value | Type | Native meaning |
|----------|-------|------|----------------|
| `PADDING` | `0x1011` | F32 | Uniform inner padding (any view) |
=== 320-370 ===
> intrinsic to the control components (a `BUTTON` is an interactive button, a
> `TOGGLE` a checkbox/switch, a `MENU` a menu), and a custom-looking button is
> expressed with `Button` + `ButtonStyle`. The renderer maps each semantic role
> onto a semantically-structured native element; control components keep their
> native element and never take an ARIA role from `ROLE`. **Headings** come from

**`STATE` enumerated values** (control/interaction state; carried as an `F32` numeric code, `value_type::F32`):

| Value | State |
|-------|-------|
| 0 | `Normal` (no special state) |
| 1 | `Disabled` |
| 2 | `Focused` |
| 3 | `Pressed` |
| 4 | `Selected` |
| 5 | `Expanded` |
| 6 | `Busy` |

`STATE` is a **semantic/accessibility** property the application sets; it never
describes visual styling (hover/press styles stay renderer/token-owned).

`STRING` properties carry their text in the frame's string section: the
property value is the *relative* offset of a length-prefixed entry, exactly as
`SET_TEXT`'s `B` field does.

separate component: `TOGGLE_STYLE` (`0x2018`, ENUM) selects the native variant —

(toggle button). The checked state is `SELECTED` (`0x2004`, U8 0/1), emitted
guest → host and reported back host → guest. The renderer owns the visual
presentation (see [Design Token System](#design-token-system)).

`SLIDER` (`0x25`) is a continuous numeric control: the guest emits its
`VALUE` plus the `MIN_VALUE`/`MAX_VALUE` range, and the renderer reports value
changes back as `VALUE_CHANGED` events (host → guest), resolving the semantic
value from its own track geometry (see [EVENT](#event-0x03--host--guest)).

own rendered-output tree. High-level interpretations — tap, drag, long-press —
are built by the guest/app from these raw inputs and are **not** part of the
protocol.

## Directions

- `TREE` / `PARAMETER` are **guest → host** (application → renderer).
- `EVENT` is **host → guest** (renderer → application): raw pointer/keyboard
  inputs with a host-resolved `targetId`. A conforming EVENT encoder/decoder
  MUST reproduce vectors 8–12 and 21–22 exactly.
- `META` is both directions.

## Frame Conformance

A complete frame is: delta opcodes written into consecutive ring slots, then a
`frameCount` increment in the header block. Ring slot `i` occupies bytes
`[ringOffset + i*16, ringOffset + i*16 + 16)`.

The header block layout and ring semantics are defined in [OPCODE.md](./OPCODE.md#linear-memory-layout).

The host → guest event ring shares the same 16-byte slot format and lives at
`eventRingOffset` (header `0x2A`), with `eventReadCursor` (0x36, guest-owned)
and `eventWriteCursor` (0x3A, host-owned). A host writing `EVENT:POINTER_UP`
into the event ring must reproduce the exact vector-11 bytes in the slot at
`eventWriteCursor`, then advance `eventWriteCursor`; the guest advances
`eventReadCursor` after draining.

String-bearing events (`TEXT_CHANGED`, `NAVIGATE` with the `NAVIGATE_URL`
flag) resolve their text from the host → guest **event arena** (header
`eventArenaOffset` 0x40 / `eventArenaCursor` 0x48, host-owned, shared memory)
or the batch's string section (network) — the same dual absolute/relative
convention as `PARAMETER::SET_TEXT`. See OPCODE.md's
[event arena](./OPCODE.md#event-arena-host--guest) section.

A network batch serializes opcodes + an arena delta (see
[OPCODE.md](./OPCODE.md#transport)). A conforming batch encoder/decoder MUST
reproduce the following bytes exactly. The header's `sequence` field is the
per-stream monotonic message sequence (see
[Sequence gap detection](./OPCODE.md#sequence-gap-detection)); the vectors below
use representative values.

190: ### Semantics
191: 
192: - **`FONT_WEIGHT`** is a numeric F32 on the 100–900 scale (`regular`≈400,
193:   `bold`≈700). Renderers map it to the nearest native weight.
194: - **`KERNING` vs `TRACKING`**: kerning adjusts per-glyph spacing at a
195:   point/em scale; tracking adds uniform letter spacing. Both are F32 points.
196: - **`LINE_LIMIT`**: a positive value clamps the rendered text to **at most N
197:   lines**, any overflow replaced by an ellipsis `…` at the end of the last
198:   visible line (tail truncation); `0`/absent = unlimited. It does not force a
199:   single line — lines form by wrapping at the available width and by explicit
200:   line breaks.
201: - **`TRUNCATION_MODE`** (`Head`=0, `Middle`=1, `Tail`=2) **positions the
202:   ellipsis** (start / middle / end of the last visible line) whenever a
203:   `LINE_LIMIT` clamp truncates. On its own it has **no observable effect**
204:   (SwiftUI-aligned) — it never forces a single line and never truncates by
205:   itself. Full contract: [LAYOUT.md](./LAYOUT.md#content-fitting-truncation--clipping).
206: - **`TEXT_ALIGNMENT`** differs from stack `ALIGNMENT`: it aligns the text block
207:   inside its own bounds, not children of a stack.

#### Window metadata

`META::SET_WINDOW_METADATA` is an **extensible field family** for presentation
metadata of the host **window/surface** that owns the stream (a browser tab, a
native window, an embedded surface). One opcode sets one field; new fields are
new ids, never new commands. The protocol defines the concept; **each renderer
maps it onto its own chrome** — the browser mapping is only one of them:

| Renderer | `TITLE` | `DESCRIPTION` | `LOCALE` |
|----------|---------|---------------|----------|
| HTML / SSR | `<title>` | `<meta name="description">` | `<html lang>` |
| DOM client | `document.title` | meta description | `<html lang>` |
| GTK4 | window/headerbar title | accessible description | — |
| Qt | window title | — | — |

| Field | Value | `B` encoding | Notes |
|-------|-------|--------------|-------|
| `TITLE` | `0x0001` | string offset | Title of the hosting window/surface |
| `DESCRIPTION` | `0x0002` | string offset | Human-readable description of the current content |
| `LOCALE` | `0x0003` | string offset | BCP 47 content locale |

The string encoding follows the same convention as `SET_TEXT`/`ROUTE`: an
absolute offset into the guest arena over the shared ring, or a *relative*
offset into the batch's string section over the network. An **empty string
clears** the field, and the renderer applies its own default. Metadata is
renderer-global (not part of the retained tree), survives `META::RESET`, and is
re-emitted in a full snapshot (`META::RESYNC`).

Semantics:

- The application owns the values; a bound signal change emits exactly the
  changed field (like a property diff).
- A proxied origin's window metadata is **ignored** — an embedded app never
  retitles the host window (spec/PROXY.md).
- Web-only artifacts (`canonical`, `robots`, sitemap) are host concerns and are
  **not** protocol fields.

## Reactive Emission

The engine emits **only what changed** relative to its previous emission:

- **Property diff**: a changed `spacing`/`padding`/`WIDTH`/`HEIGHT`/`ALIGNMENT`/
  text emits a single `SET_PROPERTY` / `SET_TEXT` for that node. (Padding is a
  styling modifier, but it still diffs and emits like any other property.)
- **Structural diff**: a node added/removed/moved emits the corresponding
  `TREE` opcode(s).
- **Steady state**: an unchanged tree emits **zero** opcodes.

The **`frame` compound modifier** (width/height/alignment) is not a distinct
protocol concept: it emits `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT`/`ALIGNMENT` as ordinary
`PARAMETER:SET_PROPERTY` deltas, exactly like any other constraint property. There
is no `frame` opcode or dedicated wire type.

Signals in the application drive this: a signal marks the tree dirty; the
engine's next `emit` reconciles and writes only the delta. The renderer applies
each frame as a delta to its native elements.

---

## Linear Memory Layout

The guest engine and host share a **single linear memory**. Regions are fixed at module start:

```
+───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────+
| 0x0000  Header block (80 B)  — cursors, frame counter, layout  |
| 0x0050  Ring buffer (16 B × slotCount)   [guest → host]        |
| ...      (slots densely packed, 64-byte aligned base)          |
| 0x10050 Event ring buffer (16 B × slotCount) [host → guest]    |
| ...                                                           |
| 0x20050 Arena (bump region, guest-owned: strings / tokens)     |
| ...                                                           |
| 0x30050 Event arena (bump region, host-owned: event strings)   |
| ...                                                            |
+───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────+
```

> The event ring is the **host → guest** direction of the shared-memory
> transport: the renderer writes `EVENT`-category opcodes here and the
> guest/app drains them. It uses the same 16-byte slot layout as the main
> (guest → host) ring; both share `slotCount` (same capacity).
>
> The **event arena** is the host-owned bump region that makes strings flow
> **host → guest** over the shared ring: a renderer bump-allocates `TEXT_CHANGED`
> text (and any future string-bearing event payload) here and references it by
> its absolute byte offset — exactly mirroring how the guest uses the guest
> arena for `SET_TEXT` / STRING properties. The host resets its cursor on
> `META::RESET`; if the event arena is full the host applies backpressure
> (drops/stalls the event), mirroring ring backpressure.

### Header block (80 bytes)

| Offset | Size | Field | Producer | Description |
|--------|------|-------|----------|-------------|
| 0x00 | 4 | `magic` | — | `0x504C504C` (`PLPL`) |
| 0x04 | 2 | `version` | — | Wire protocol version (1) |
| 0x06 | 4 | `ringOffset` | — | Byte offset of the ring region |
| 0x0A | 4 | `ringBytes` | — | Byte length of the ring region |
| 0x0E | 4 | `slotCount` | — | Number of ring slots (power of two) |
| 0x12 | 4 | `arenaOffset` | — | Byte offset of the arena region |
| 0x16 | 4 | `arenaBytes` | — | Byte length of the arena region |
| 0x1A | 4 | `arenaCursor` | guest | Next free byte in the arena |
| 0x1E | 4 | `readCursor` | host | Ring slot the host has consumed up to |
| 0x22 | 4 | `writeCursor` | guest | Ring slot the guest has written up to |
| 0x26 | 4 | `frameCount` | guest | Monotonic completed-frame counter |
| 0x2A | 4 | `eventRingOffset` | — | Byte offset of the host→guest event ring region |
| 0x2E | 4 | `eventRingBytes` | — | Byte length of the event ring region |
| 0x32 | 4 | `eventSlotCount` | — | Event ring slot count (power of two; = `slotCount`) |
| 0x36 | 4 | `eventReadCursor` | guest | Event ring slot the guest has consumed up to |
| 0x3A | 4 | `eventWriteCursor` | host | Event ring slot the host has written up to |
| 0x40 | 4 | `eventArenaOffset` | — | Byte offset of the host→guest event arena region |
| 0x44 | 4 | `eventArenaBytes` | — | Byte length of the event arena region |
| 0x48 | 4 | `eventArenaCursor` | host | Next free byte in the event arena |

### Ring buffer

- Contiguous array of **16-byte slots**; `slotCount` is a **power of two** (wrap via mask, no modulo).
- **Producer** (guest) writes at `writeCursor`, then advances `writeCursor` and increments `frameCount` at frame end.
- **Consumer** (host) reads from `readCursor` up to `writeCursor`; after draining a frame it advances `readCursor`.
- **Backpressure**: the producer must not advance `writeCursor` past `readCursor` (ring full). The producer SHOULD flush a frame before the ring is full.
- **Frame boundary detection**: the host watches `frameCount`. When it advances, exactly one frame (all slots from the previously consumed `readCursor` to the current `writeCursor`) is complete.

### Event ring (host → guest)

- The **host** (renderer) is the producer: it writes `EVENT`-category opcodes at `eventWriteCursor`.
- The **guest** (app/engine) is the consumer: it reads from `eventReadCursor` up to `eventWriteCursor`, then advances `eventReadCursor`.
- Events are raw inputs and are consumed as soon as they are written (no frame batching); `eventFrameCount` is not required.
- Backpressure mirrors the main ring: the host must not advance `eventWriteCursor` past `eventReadCursor`.

### Arena

- A pre-allocated **bump region** for variable-length data (strings, token paths).
- Every arena entry is **self-describing**: `[u32 byteLength][bytes...]`.
- Opcodes reference entries by their **byte offset** (`arenaRef`), so an entry's length is read directly from the arena — all opcodes stay 16 bytes.
- The guest advances `arenaCursor` monotonically (no free-list, no fragmentation). The arena MAY be reset via `META::RESET`.

### Event arena (host → guest)

The event arena is the **host-owned mirror** of the arena, giving the shared-memory
transport a host → guest string section so strings flow **both ways on all
transports**:

- The **host** (renderer) bump-allocates event string payloads here (e.g. the
  new text of a `TEXT_CHANGED`) and references them by their **absolute byte
  offset** in the event opcode — the same `SET_TEXT` shared-memory convention
  used in the guest arena.
- The **guest** resolves the text from the event arena region when draining
  events (`EVENT::TEXT_CHANGED`).
- Entries share the same self-describing `[u32 byteLength][bytes...]` layout as
  the guest arena.
- The host advances `eventArenaCursor` monotonically and resets it on
  `META::RESET`; a full event arena is backpressure (the host drops/stalls the
  event until the guest drains or a reset lands).
- Over the **network**, host → guest string payloads use the batch's string
  section with *relative* offsets instead (see [Transport](#transport)) — the
  same dual absolute/relative convention as `SET_TEXT`.

---

## Colors

Literal colors are **sRGB** (IEC 61966-2-1, D65 white point), packed as `0xAARRGGBB`:

- `AA`: alpha (0x00 transparent – 0xFF opaque)
- `RR`: red, `GG`: green, `BB`: blue

Stored little-endian in a `u32` payload. A color **property** may alternatively carry a `DESIGN_TOKEN` reference to a token path instead of a literal (see [Design Token System](#design-token-system)); semantic token resolution and theme adaptation remain **renderer-owned**.

            <artifactId>kotlin-stdlib</artifactId>
            <version>${kotlin.version}</version>
            <scope>test</scope>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>dev.pathland</groupId>
            <artifactId>pathland-view-core</artifactId>
            <version>${project.version}</version>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>net.java.dev.jna</groupId>
            <artifactId>jna</artifactId>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.junit.jupiter</groupId>
            <artifactId>junit-jupiter</artifactId>
            <scope>test</scope>
        </dependency>
    </dependencies>

    <build>
        <plugins>
            <plugin>
                <groupId>org.jetbrains.kotlin</groupId>
                <artifactId>kotlin-maven-plugin</artifactId>
                <version>${kotlin.version}</version>
                <executions>
                    <execution>
                        <id>test-compile</id>
                        <phase>process-test-sources</phase>
                        <goals><goal>test-compile</goal></goals>
                        <configuration>
                            <sourceDirs>
                                <sourceDir>${project.basedir}/src/test/kotlin</sourceDir>
                            </sourceDirs>
                        </configuration>
                    </execution>
                </executions>
                <configuration>
                    <jvmTarget>${maven.compiler.release}</jvmTarget>
                    <languageVersion>2.4</languageVersion>
                    <apiVersion>2.4</apiVersion>
                </configuration>
            </plugin>
            <plugin>
                <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                <artifactId>maven-surefire-plugin</artifactId>
                <configuration>
                    <!-- Point the test JVM at the Rust renderer cdylib; absent the
                         dylib, the shim tests are skipped via an assumption. -->
                    <argLine>-Djava.library.path=${project.basedir}/../../rust/target/debug</argLine>
                </configuration>
            </plugin>

            <!-- Embed the Rust renderer dylib in the jar so it travels with the
                 artifact (JNA extracts it at runtime — no java.library.path needed).
                 Copies the host-platform build into META-INF/native/. Fails loudly
                 when the dylib is missing (the CI rust job builds it; locally run
                 cargo build first). -->
            <plugin>
                <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                <artifactId>maven-antrun-plugin</artifactId>
                <executions>
                    <execution>
                        <id>embed-native-renderer</id>
                        <phase>process-resources</phase>
                        <configuration>
                            <target>
                                <!-- Determine the platform library extension. -->
                                <condition property="pathland.native.ext" value=".dylib">
                                    <os family="mac" />
                                </condition>
                                <condition property="pathland.native.ext" value=".dll">
                                    <os family="windows" />
                                </condition>
                                <condition property="pathland.native.ext" value=".so">
                                    <os family="unix" />
                                </condition>
                                <property name="pathland.native.ext" value="" />

                                <!-- Release builds stage one lib per platform under
                                     target/native/<os>-<arch>/ (the CI matrix) and
                                     this copies each into META-INF/native/<os>-<arch>/.
                                     A local build has no staging dir and instead
                                     embeds the host Rust debug build in the flat
                                     META-INF/native/ layout. -->
                                <property name="pathland.native.staging" value="${project.basedir}/target/native" />
                                <available file="${pathland.native.staging}" type="dir" property="pathland.native.staged" />
                                <property name="pathland.native.host" value="${project.basedir}/../../rust/target/debug/libpathland_render_html${pathland.native.ext}" />
                                <available file="${pathland.native.host}" property="pathland.native.host.present" />

                                <fail message="No Rust renderer library to embed: neither per-platform libs at ${pathland.native.staging}/<os>-<arch>/ (release) nor the host build at ${pathland.native.host} (local). Build it first: cargo build -p pathland-render-html (in lib/rust).">
                                    <condition>
                                        <and>
                                            <not><isset property="pathland.native.staged" /></not>
                                            <not><isset property="pathland.native.host.present" /></not>
                                        </and>
                                    </condition>
                                </fail>

                                <mkdir dir="${project.build.outputDirectory}/META-INF/native" />
                                <!-- Release: copy each staged platform dir verbatim. -->
                                <copy todir="${project.build.outputDirectory}/META-INF/native">
                                    <fileset dir="${pathland.native.staging}" includes="*/*" erroronmissingdir="false" />
                                </copy>
                                <!-- Local dev: embed the host lib in the flat layout. -->
                                <copy file="${pathland.native.host}"
                                      tofile="${project.build.outputDirectory}/META-INF/native/libpathland_render_html${pathland.native.ext}"
                                      failonerror="false" />
                            </target>
                        </configuration>
                        <goals>
                            <goal>run</goal>
                        </goals>
                    </execution>
                </executions>
            </plugin>
        </plugins>
    </build>
</project>

# Verify the no_std / wasm32 direction guard: `pathland-core` and `pathland-view`
# must stay `#![no_std]` + `alloc` and compile for `wasm32-unknown-unknown`.

# desktop path (`pathland-view-native`) is the only consumer today, but the core
# must not become desktop-only.

# pathland-core — implementation status

**Last updated:** October 27, 2026

The **protocol core**: 16-byte opcode, SPSC ring buffers (both directions),
bump arenas (both directions), memory layout, typed events, and the golden
conformance vectors. The protocol contract is defined in `spec/`; this file
tracks what this crate implements.

## Implemented

- **Window/surface metadata** (`META::SET_WINDOW_METADATA` 0x08, draft): an extensible field family (`TITLE`, `DESCRIPTION`, `LOCALE`) for the hosting window/surface, plus the shared no_std `WindowMeta` decoder helper. Spec + conformance vectors 44–45.

- **Component types** (`constants.rs::component_type`): the full grouped map —
  `TEXT 0x01, IMAGE 0x02, COLOR 0x03, SHAPE 0x04, DIVIDER 0x05, SPACER 0x06,
  PROGRESS_VIEW 0x07, GAUGE 0x08, VIDEO 0x0A, ICON 0x0B, VSTACK 0x10, HSTACK 0x11, ZSTACK 0x12, GRID
0x13, SCROLLVIEW 0x14, LAZY_VGRID 0x15, LAZY_HGRID 0x16, LAZY_VSTACK 0x1B,
   LAZY_HSTACK 0x1C, GRID_ROW 0x1D, PROXY_VIEW 0x1E, BUTTON 0x20, TEXT_FIELD 0x21, TEXT_EDITOR 0x22, TOGGLE
   0x24, SLIDER 0x25, STEPPER 0x26, DATE_PICKER 0x27, PICKER 0x28, MENU 0x29,
   COLOR_PICKER 0x2A, MEDIA_CONTROLLER 0x30, COMMENT 0x7F`. (`0x09` formerly
   `AUDIO` is freed — audio has no view; spec/MEDIA.md.)
- **Media kit** (spec/MEDIA.md): `MEDIA_CONTROLLER` (`0x30`, **non-visual**,
  layout-transparent) owns the resource + transport; a `VIDEO` (`0x0A`) surface
  references it via `MEDIA_CONTROLLER_ID` (`0x103A`). Transport properties
  `PLAYBACK_STATE` (0x1035), `MEDIA_POSITION` (0x1036), `MEDIA_VOLUME` (0x1037),
  `MEDIA_SOURCE` (0x103B), `MEDIA_MUTED` (0x103C), `MEDIA_LOOP` (0x103D),
  `MEDIA_RATE` (0x103E); the `MEDIA_*` events target the **controller** id and add
  `MEDIA_DURATION_CHANGED` (0x14). Covered by conformance vectors 39–41.
- **`PROXY_VIEW`** (`0x1E`) — a container whose child subtree is served by another
  Pathland server (spec/PROXY.md); the id is the only wire-visible part of the
  proxy contract (the origin subtree's nodes are ordinary opcodes with
  **id-remapped** node ids). Covered by conformance vector 38.
- **`GRID_COLUMNS`/`GRID_ROWS`** (`0x001E`/`0x001F`, F32) track-count properties
  for grids (positive = count, `FILL`/absent = auto-fit; never a pixel box),
  **`GRID_TRACKS`** (`0x0020`, STRING) per-track specs (takes precedence over the
  counts), and the **`GRID_ROW`** (`0x1D`) component (a grid child whose children

## Plan — Issue #98: AttributedString + inline Markdown

I could not create the branch because plan mode is read-only; step 0 below runs after approval. I also confirmed issue #98 is the rich-text issue, not a website task.

### Decisions locked in
- **Branch:** `feat/attributed-string-markdown` off `main`.
- **Command ID:** `PARAMETER::SET_ATTRIBUTED_TEXT = 0x05` (not `0x04`; `SET_DATE` already owns `0x04`). A separate follow-up issue will cover regrouping the PARAMETER command IDs.
- **Links:** render-only v1 (`<a href>` / Pango link markup); no link-activation event.
- **Qt:** deferred; Qt falls back to plain text. Status note only.
- **Offsets:** UTF-8 **byte** offsets into the text (Pango-native; DOM converts to UTF-16 when needed).

---

### 1. Protocol (spec first)

**`spec/OPCODE.md`**
- Add `SET_ATTRIBUTED_TEXT` to the PARAMETER table: `A=nodeId`, `B=arenaRef` (shared memory) / relative string-section offset (network), `C=0`.
- Add an "Attributed text payload" section. Proposed entry (inside the arena's `[u32 byteLength][bytes]` wrapper):

```
[u32 textByteLen][utf8 text]
[u32 runCount]
  run:
    [u32 start][u32 end][u32 attrCount]
    attr:
      [u16 propId][u8 valueType][u8 reserved][u32 value]
[u32 linkCount]
  link:
    [u32 start][u32 end][u32 urlByteLen][utf8 url]
```

- `valueType` reuses the standard codes (`U8/U32/I32/F32/ENUM/COLOR`); STRING/DESIGN_TOKEN/LIST are invalid inside runs in v1.
- Semantics: node-level properties remain the base; runs override ranges; overlapping runs apply in wire order (later wins per property); links are separate, last covering link wins; ranges are `[start,end)`, validated against text length and UTF-8 boundaries.
- Renderers that do not support rich text render the payload's plain text (fallback guarantee).
- Note the deviation from the issue's 6-byte attribute: the extra value-type byte makes decoding deterministic and forward-compatible; counts/URL lengths are `u32`.

**Companion specs**
- `spec/MODIFIERS.md` §Text Formatting: note run attributes reuse the same property vocabulary.
- `spec/PRIMITIVES.md` §TEXT: rich content arrives via `SET_ATTRIBUTED_TEXT`.
- `spec/DSL.md`: `AttributedString`, `Text(AttributedString)`, `Markdown.parse`.
- `spec/ENGINE.md`: emission order/diff rule (attributed text replaces `SET_TEXT`; plain fallback rule).
- `spec/CONFORMANCE.md` + `pathland-core/src/conformance.rs`: exact golden bytes for a small payload (e.g. `"ab"` + one bold run + one link).

### 2. Core model + codec

**New `pathland-core/src/attributed.rs`** (`no_std` + `alloc`, no deps):
- `AttributedString { text, runs, links }`, `StyleRun`, `LinkRun`, typed `AttrValue`.
- `encode_into(&mut Vec<u8>)`, `decode(&[u8]) -> Result<...>`, validation, `PartialEq`, builders.
- Bounds-checked decoding; malformed payloads are rejected, never panic.

**Core API**
- `constants.rs`: `parameter::SET_ATTRIBUTED_TEXT = 0x05`.
- `ring.rs`: `push_set_attributed_text` next to `push_set_text`.
- `lib.rs`: `Guest::set_attributed_text` (encode → arena alloc → push).
- Tests: round-trip, empty runs, overlap, UTF-8 boundaries, truncated/oversized payloads, arena-full behavior.
- No new C-ABI function required: `pathland_ring_buffer_push` + `arena_alloc` already support it; note in status.

### 3. Shared Markdown parser

**New crate `lib/rust/crates/pathland-markdown`** (`no_std` + `alloc`, depends on `pathland-core`):
- Inline subset: `**bold**`, `*italic*`, `` `code` ``, `~~strikethrough~~`, `[label](url)`.
- Nesting + backslash escapes; code spans disable inner parsing; links separate from style runs.
- `cdylib` C ABI: `pathland_markdown_parse(ptr,len) -> *mut u8` returning the encoded payload + length; `pathland_markdown_free(ptr)`.
- Unit tests for parsing, nesting, escaping, UTF-8, malformed input.
- Add to workspace, CI build/artifact, release native matrix; add to `check-wasm.sh` if we want the parser covered by the wasm guard.

### 4. Retained engine + DSLs

**Rust**
- `pathland-engine/src/node.rs`: add `attributed_text: Option<AttributedString>` and `attributed_binding: Option<SignalId>` on `Node` (keep `Component::Text` as the plain fallback; avoids breaking every constructor/match).
- `signal.rs`: `SignalValue::Attributed(AttributedString)` + `Dep::AttributedText { node }`.
- `engine.rs`:
  - `SnapshotNode.attributed: Option<(AttributedString, u32)>` (value + reusable arena offset).
  - Mount/delta: if attributed present, emit `SET_ATTRIBUTED_TEXT` instead of `SET_TEXT`; unchanged value reuses the arena offset and emits zero opcodes; switching back to plain emits `SET_TEXT`.
  - `emit_cell`: partial emit for `Dep::AttributedText`.
- `pathland-view`: `Text::attributed(...)`, `Text::markdown(...)`, `TextConfig` additions; tests for mount, signal delta, zero re-emit.

**Kotlin/JVM**
- `pathland-view-core`: pure-Kotlin `AttributedString` + range-tracking builder; `PathlandNode.attributedText/attributedBinding`; `Views.kt` `Text(AttributedString)` / `Text(Signal<AttributedString>)`.
- `Emitter`: emit/reconcile/signal effect for attributed text.
- `OpcodeSink.setAttributedText`; `FrameOpcodeSink` (relative string-section offset) and `RingOpcodeSink` (absolute arena offset).
- **New `lib/java/pathland-markdown` module** mirroring `pathland-render-html`: `dev.pathland.markdown.Markdown.parse(String): AttributedString`, JNA loader with `META-INF/native` embedding. Separate artifact keeps the native dependency opt-in (alternative: put it in `pathland-view-core`, but that makes JNA mandatory for all hosts).
- Register the module in `lib/java/pom.xml`; add CI/release staging.

### 5. Transport + generated artifacts

- JVM `FrameRebase`: rebase `SET_ATTRIBUTED_TEXT`'s `B` offset (same as `SET_TEXT`).
- JVM `ProxyIdMap`: include the new command in node-id remapping (`A`).
- Rust `pathland-engine-golden::used_arena`: add the new command so its payload survives fixtures; add a scenario.
- `pathland-protocol-manifest`: add the command row; regenerate `spec/protocol.tsv`.
- `pathland-ts-codegen`: add `CMD_SET_ATTRIBUTED_TEXT`; regenerate via `npm run regen`.
- Server tests: delta batching/rebase, proxy id remap.

### 6. Renderers

**Shared `pathland-render-core`**
- `HostNode.attributed: Option<AttributedString>`; decode `SET_ATTRIBUTED_TEXT` from `frame.arena_get(op.b())` into both `attributed` and plain `text`; add a `describe` arm.

**GTK (`pathland-render-gtk`)**
- Use `GtkLabel::set_markup` for attributed text. Pango 0.20 has no `PANGO_ATTR_LINK` binding, so the issue's `PANGO_ATTR_LINK` is not available; Pango markup supports `<a href>`, `<span>`, weight/style/size/foreground/underline/strikethrough. This is the clean renderer-owned solution for v1.
- Build segments from runs/links; fold node-level base styles into the outer span; escape markup.
- Keep the existing `AttrList` path for plain text. Links are styled and inert (render-only).
- Tests: label plain text, markup contains expected spans/anchors, escaping.

**SSR HTML (`pathland-render-html`)**
- `Node.attributed`; decode from the binary string-section entry (add a bytes helper, not `strings_str`).
- Render `TEXT` by splitting at all run/link boundaries into non-overlapping segments; each segment becomes `<span style>` or `<a href style>`; escape text/URLs; reuse/factor the inline-style mapping from `Node::style_css`.
- Preserve the outer `data-pathland-id`/role/aria attributes. Add tests and golden fixtures.

**DOM client (`lib/typescript`)**
- Add `CMD_SET_ATTRIBUTED_TEXT` + a binary payload decoder (`attributed.ts`).
- `apply.ts`: on the new command, rebuild the text container's inner segments (spans/anchors). Mark the container `pathland-rich-text` so `PROP_TEXT`/`LABEL` updates never wipe rich content.
- Optional fast path (issue's intent): when the text is unchanged and only ranges changed, use `createRange`/`splitText`/`surroundContents`; fall back to rebuild when ranges cross element boundaries or are invalid. Ship the correct rebuild path first, add the fast path behind tests.
- Hydration: keep the SSR spans/anchors; map deltas by the outer element id.
- Tests: apply rich text, escaping, link href, text delta, style-only delta, fallback.

**Qt**
- No change; `HostNode.text` is populated from the payload so Qt renders plain text. Add a status note.

### 7. Tests + verification

```bash
cd lib/rust && cargo test
cargo run -p pathland-engine-golden -- --emit && cargo run -p pathland-engine-golden -- --check
cargo run -p pathland-protocol-manifest
npm --prefix lib/typescript run regen
cargo build -p pathland-render-html -p pathland-markdown
cd lib/typescript && npm run typecheck && npm test && npm run build
cd lib/java && mvn install
lib/rust/check-wasm.sh
```

### 8. Status/docs to update

`pathland-core`, `pathland-engine`, `pathland-view`, `pathland-render-core`, `pathland-render-gtk`, `pathland-render-html`, `pathland-render-qt` (deferred note), `pathland-engine-golden`, `pathland-protocol-manifest`, `pathland-ts-codegen`, `pathland-html-golden`, `lib/typescript`, `pathland-view-core`, `pathland-server-core`, new `pathland-markdown` (Rust + Java).

### 9. Follow-ups / out of scope

- Create the follow-up issue for PARAMETER command-ID regrouping.
- Link activation event (`EVENT::LINK_ACTIVATED`) for desktop/SPA routing.
- Qt rich-text rendering.
- Nested/block Markdown (only inline v1), images in Markdown, custom run attributes beyond the text-format catalog.

### Execution order

0. Create branch `feat/attributed-string-markdown` (and the follow-up command-ID issue).
1. Spec + conformance vector.
2. Core model/codec + tests.
3. `pathland-markdown` crate + C ABI.
4. Rust engine/DSL + JVM DSL/emitter + JVM markdown shim.
5. Transport/rebase/proxy + generated artifacts.
6. Render-core, GTK, SSR, DOM.
7. Full test/regeneration/status pass.

Rich-text runs will carry **scalar text-format attributes** from the existing modifier catalog, not arbitrary CSS/style objects. Node-level text properties remain the base; a run overrides only the ranges it covers. Links are a **separate** section (URL only, no style attributes).

### V1 run attributes (recommended)

| Attribute | ID | Wire type | Markdown source | GTK mapping | SSR / DOM mapping |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `FONT_WEIGHT` | `0x1008` | F32 (100–900) | `**bold**` → 700 | `weight` | `font-weight` |
| `FONT_STYLE` | `0x1017` | F32 enum (`Normal`=0, `Italic`=1) | `*italic*` | `style` | `font-style` |
| `FONT_DESIGN` | `0x1018` | F32 enum (`Default`/`Serif`/`Rounded`/`Monospaced`) | `` `code` `` → Monospaced | `font_family` | `font-family` |
| `FONT_SIZE` | `0x1007` | F32 points | builder only | `size` | `font-size` |
| `COLOR` | `0x100A` | COLOR `0xAARRGGBB` | builder only | `foreground` | `color` |
| `UNDERLINE` | `0x101F` | U8 0/1 | builder only | `underline` | `text-decoration` |
| `STRIKETHROUGH` | `0x1020` | U8 0/1 | `~~strike~~` | `strikethrough` | `text-decoration` |
| **Link URL** | — | string (link section) | `[text](url)` | Pango link markup | `<a href>` |

### Extended scalar attributes (same payload, no wire change)
These can be allowed in the builder and are renderer-best-effort:

| Attribute | ID | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `BACKGROUND_COLOR` | `0x1001` | COLOR | `<span>` background; Pango `background` |
| `FONT_WIDTH` | `0x1019` | F32 | Pango `stretch` / CSS `font-stretch` |
| `KERNING` | `0x101A` | F32 | CSS `letter-spacing`; Pango approximates with `letter_spacing` |
| `TRACKING` | `0x101B` | F32 | CSS `letter-spacing`; Pango `letter_spacing` |
| `BASELINE_OFFSET` | `0x101C` | F32 | Pango `rise`; CSS `vertical-align` |
| `TEXT_CASE` | `0x101E` | F32 enum | CSS `text-transform`; GTK may ignore |

### Explicitly not in v1
- **`FONT_FAMILY`** (`0x1009`) as a run attribute — it is a `STRING`; runs only carry 4-byte scalars. It stays node-level. Could be added later as a run attribute with an arena string offset.
- **`TEXT_STYLE`** (`0x1032`) per run — node-level typography; per-run size/weight is enough.
- **`LINE_SPACING`** per run — inherently line-level, not range-level.
- **Custom link attributes** (`target`, `rel`, per-link color) — URL only; renderers own link styling.
- Shadows/effects, design-token references, nested/block Markdown, images, link-activation events.

The wire format already carries a `valueType` byte per attribute, so adding the extended scalar set later does not change the payload or command.

Do you want the **focused V1 set** (the first table + links) or should the builder expose the **extended scalar set** from day one (renderer-best-effort)?
Lets go with with the focusd v1

Focused V1 it is. Final plan is locked:

### Attributes in rich-text runs (V1)
- `FONT_WEIGHT` `0x1008` — F32 (100–900)
- `FONT_STYLE` `0x1017` — F32 enum (`Normal`=0, `Italic`=1)
- `FONT_DESIGN` `0x1018` — F32 enum (`Default`/`Serif`/`Rounded`/`Monospaced`)
- `FONT_SIZE` `0x1007` — F32 points
- `COLOR` `0x100A` — COLOR `0xAARRGGBB`
- `UNDERLINE` `0x101F` — U8 0/1
- `STRIKETHROUGH` `0x1020` — U8 0/1
- **Link URL** — separate link section, render-only

The payload keeps the per-attribute `valueType` byte (so the extended set can be added later without a wire change), but the builder/spec/parser expose only the seven scalar attributes above. `FONT_FAMILY`, `TEXT_STYLE`, `LINE_SPACING`, shadows/effects, and per-link attributes are explicitly out of scope.

### PARAMETER (0x02)

The engine does not emit positions. `PARAMETER` carries the **constraint properties**
that native renderers feed to their own layout — spacing, alignment, FILL/HUG
size hints — plus **styling modifiers** (padding, colors, fonts, borders).

| Command | Value | A | B | C | Flags | Description |
|---------|-------|---|---|---|-------|-------------|
| `SET_PROPERTY` | `0x01` | nodeId | propertyId (u16, low) + valueType (u8, high byte) | value | — | Set a constraint/style property; `value` depends on `valueType` |
| `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` | `0x02` | arenaRef (path) | valueType (u8) | value | — | Override a design token; path is an arena string |
| `SET_TEXT` | `0x03` | nodeId | arenaRef (utf8) | 0 | — | Set a node's text content |
| `SET_DATE` | `0x04` | nodeId | days since epoch (I32) | millis of day (U32) | — | Set a node's date value (e.g. a `DATE_PICKER`); see [EVENTS.md](./EVENTS.md#date) for the matching `DATE_CHANGED` event |

`SET_PROPERTY` encodes the value type in the **high byte of `B`** (bits 24–31) and the property id in the low two bytes:

```
B = (valueType << 16) | propertyId
```

#### Value types

| Value Type | Value | C / value encoding |
|------------|-------|--------------------|
| `U8` | `0x01` | low byte of C |
| `U32` | `0x02` | u32 |
| `I32` | `0x03` | i32 |
| `F32` | `0x04` | f32 |
| `STRING` | `0x05` | arenaRef (utf8) |
| `ENUM` | `0x06` | low byte of C |
| `COLOR` | `0x07` | packed `0xAARRGGBB` |
| `DESIGN_TOKEN` | `0x08` | arenaRef (token path) |
| `LIST` | `0x09` | arenaRef (length-prefixed array, see below) |

> **Enum-valued properties** (`ALIGNMENT`, `TEXT_ALIGNMENT`, `TRUNCATION_MODE`,
> `ROLE`, `STATE`, and the draft `FONT_*`/`CONTENT_MODE`/`CONTROL_SIZE`/`SHAPE_KIND`
> properties) are carried with the **`F32` value type**, holding the numeric enum
> code as an f32 bit pattern (e.g. `ALIGNMENT=Center(1)` → `C = 1.0f32.to_bits()`).
> The enumerated code tables live in
> [MODIFIERS.md](./MODIFIERS.md#appendix-enumerated-values). The `ENUM` value type
> (low byte of `C`) is available for explicitly `ENUM`-coded properties.
>
> **Token references**: any property that normally carries a `COLOR` / `F32` /
> `STRING` / `ENUM` value MAY instead carry the `DESIGN_TOKEN` value type, with
> `C` = arenaRef to a token path (see [Design Token System](#design-token-system)
> and [TOKENS.md](./TOKENS.md)).
>
> **`LIST` arrays**: a `LIST` value (`C` = arenaRef) is a length-prefixed array in
> the string arena: `[u32 count][element × count]`, each element a `u32` holding
> the value-type's bit pattern — currently produced with each element a `F32`
> (the `FIT_QUERY` threshold table), so `bytes = 4 + 4·count`. The count is the
> first `u32` (little-endian); a zero count is an empty list. Decoders read the
> element count, never infer it from the arena length, so a property can re-emit
> a shorter list with the arena entry intact.

#### Constraint properties for native layout

The following properties drive native layout; the renderer maps them to its
native layout properties (e.g. `SPACING` → a gap between children,
`WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` → size requests). Special `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` values: `-1` = FILL
(expand to available), `-2` = HUG_CONTENT (native intrinsic size).

## 4. Canonical mount order

For each node, before its children:

1. `TREE::CREATE_NODE`
2. `TREE::INSERT_CHILD` (when the node has a parent)
3. node properties (`PARAMETER::SET_PROPERTY`, including token/string/list
   properties)
4. node text (`PARAMETER::SET_TEXT`) and date (`PARAMETER::SET_DATE`)
5. recurse into children, in child order

The child is attached **before** its own content/properties, so an id-keyed
renderer can create and place the native element before applying content.

The trace fixtures assert this order. Property ordering within a node is
deterministic and follows the engine's stored property order.

---

## 5. Reactive emission

The engine records which nodes read each signal during emission:

- a text binding (`node.text_binding`);
- a property binding (`node.property_bindings`);
- a string-property binding (`node.string_bindings`).

When a signal changes, only the bound nodes re-emit:

- text → `PARAMETER::SET_TEXT`
- property → `PARAMETER::SET_PROPERTY`
- string property → `PARAMETER::SET_PROPERTY` with the `STRING` value type

An unrelated signal change emits nothing. A write that does not change the
signal value emits nothing.

### Zero-op recompute

An unchanged tree or unchanged signal MUST emit **zero** opcodes and MUST NOT
produce a new frame. This is the steady-state contract that makes the ring
zero-allocation during idle re-renders.

#### Attributed text payload (`SET_ATTRIBUTED_TEXT`)

`PARAMETER::SET_ATTRIBUTED_TEXT` (`0x05`) sets a node's text together with
range-scoped style runs and links. The opcode stays 16 bytes: `B` references a
single length-prefixed arena entry (absolute offset over the shared ring,
*relative* offset into the batch's string section over the network — the same
dual convention as `SET_TEXT`). The payload is binary, not UTF-8:

```
[u32 textByteLen][utf8 text]
[u32 runCount]
  repeat runCount:
    [u32 start][u32 end][u32 attrCount]
    repeat attrCount:
      [u16 propId][u8 valueType][u8 reserved = 0][u32 value]
[u32 linkCount]
  repeat linkCount:
    [u32 start][u32 end][u32 urlByteLen][utf8 url]
```

All integers are little-endian. `start`/`end` are **UTF-8 byte offsets** into
`text`, half-open `[start, end)`. A decoder MUST reject (ignore the opcode) when
a range is not on a UTF-8 boundary or `end > textByteLen`.

Style runs carry the **text-format property vocabulary** from
[MODIFIERS.md](./MODIFIERS.md#2-text-formatting). V1 allows these scalar
attributes only:

| Property | ID | `valueType` | Value |
|----------|----|-------------|-------|
| `FONT_SIZE` | `0x1007` | `F32` (`0x04`) | points |
| `FONT_WEIGHT` | `0x1008` | `F32` (`0x04`) | 100–900 |
| `COLOR` | `0x100A` | `COLOR` (`0x07`) | `0xAARRGGBB` |
| `FONT_STYLE` | `0x1017` | `F32` (`0x04`) | `Normal`=0, `Italic`=1 |
| `FONT_DESIGN` | `0x1018` | `F32` (`0x04`) | `Default`=0, `Serif`=1, `Rounded`=2, `Monospaced`=3 |
| `UNDERLINE` | `0x101F` | `U8` (`0x01`) | `0`/`1` |
| `STRIKETHROUGH` | `0x1020` | `U8` (`0x01`) | `0`/`1` |

`FONT_FAMILY` (`STRING`), `TEXT_STYLE`, `LINE_SPACING`, design-token references,
and effects are **not** valid run attributes in v1 (runs carry scalar values

        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4

  like a stack with one child) and lays out the (id-remapped) origin subtree the
  proxying server spliced in — the renderer holds no notion of "remote"
  (spec/PROXY.md §5). Without this arm the component fell to the `_ => String::new()`
  default and the spliced subtree was dropped. Covered by a unit test.
- **Stateless streaming API**: `HtmlRenderer::render_document(opcodes, strings, root)`
  / `render_fragment(...)` build a transient decode map per call and stream HTML;
  the retained `apply`/`apply_frame`/`render` model is removed.

# pathland-markdown — implementation status

**Last updated:** November 6, 2026

The **shared inline Markdown parser**: `no_std` + `alloc`, used by the Rust DSL
directly and by foreign hosts through `pathland-markdown-capi`. It produces a
`pathland_core::AttributedString` (style runs + links), not a separate AST.

## Implemented

- Inline subset: `**bold**` → `FONT_WEIGHT` 700, `*italic*` → `FONT_STYLE`
  Italic, `` `code` `` → `FONT_DESIGN` Monospaced, `~~strikethrough~~` →
  `STRIKETHROUGH`, `[label](url)` → link run (label parsed recursively), and
  backslash escapes.
- Nested emphasis with asterisk-run splitting (`***` closes italic then bold).
- UTF-8 byte offsets in the produced runs; code spans do not parse inner markup.
- Unit tests for markers, nesting, links, code, escapes, unmatched markers, and
  UTF-8 offsets.

## Not implemented / gaps

- Block Markdown (headings, lists, paragraphs), reference links, images, and
  tables.
- Underscore emphasis (`_emphasis_`); only `*` forms are recognized.

# pathland-markdown-capi — implementation status

**Last updated:** November 6, 2026

The C ABI (`cdylib` name `libpathland_markdown`) for foreign hosts (Java/JNA,
Swift, …). It wraps the shared `pathland-markdown` parser.

## Implemented

- `pathland_markdown_parse(input, len, outLen)` — returns an owned buffer with
  the encoded `AttributedString` payload; null on invalid UTF-8 / encode failure.
- `pathland_markdown_free(ptr, len)` — releases the buffer.
- Tests for round-trip and invalid UTF-8.

## Not implemented / gaps

- No streaming/incremental parse API; one call per document.

# pathland-markdown (Java) — implementation status

**Last updated:** November 6, 2026

The Java binding to the shared Rust Markdown parser (`dev.pathland.markdown`).
A JNA shim over `libpathland_markdown`; the jar embeds the cdylib under
`META-INF/native/` (the `pathland-render-html` pattern).

## Implemented

- `Markdown.parse(String): AttributedString` — the same inline parser the Rust
  DSL uses; results decode into the pure-Java `dev.pathland.view.core.AttributedString`.
- `Markdown.isAvailable()` for graceful degradation when the native library is
  absent (the test suite skips).
- Native resolution: `pathland.markdown.lib` override → jar-embedded dylib →
  local Rust debug build → `java.library.path`.
- `mvn` `process-resources` embeds the host build or the staged release natives.

## Not implemented / gaps

- The module is not yet listed in the demo app dependencies; apps opt in by
  adding `dev.pathland:pathland-markdown` when they want `Markdown.parse`.
- Block-level Markdown is not supported (it shares the inline parser).

## Kotlin usage

### 1. Static attributed text

```kotlin
import dev.pathland.view.core.AttributedString
import dev.pathland.view.dsl.Text
import dev.pathland.view.dsl.VStack

val rich = AttributedString.builder()
    .append("Hello ")
    .bold(0, 5)
    .append("world")
    .italic(6, 11)
    .color(6, 11, 0xFF2563EB.toInt())
    .link(6, 11, "https://pathland.dev")
    .build()

override fun body(): View =
    VStack(spacing = 8f) {
        Text(rich)
    }
```

Builder ranges are **Kotlin character indices**; they are converted to UTF-8 byte offsets automatically when the builder is built.

### 2. Inline Markdown

Add the module dependency (only needed for `Markdown.parse`):

```xml
<dependency>
    <groupId>dev.pathland</groupId>
    <artifactId>pathland-markdown</artifactId>
    <version>${project.version}</version>
</dependency>
```

Then:

```kotlin
import dev.pathland.markdown.Markdown
import dev.pathland.view.dsl.Text

Text(Markdown.parse("**Bold**, *italic*, `code`, ~~gone~~, and [a link](https://pathland.dev)"))
```

The parser is the shared Rust one; the jar embeds `libpathland_markdown`. Locally build it first with:

```bash
cd lib/rust && cargo build -p pathland-markdown-capi
```

or use `mvn -P refresh-ide validate`.

### 3. Reactive attributed text

```kotlin
import dev.pathland.view.dsl.*
import dev.pathland.markdown.Markdown

private val message = signal(Markdown.parse("**loading**"))

override fun body(): View =
    Text(message)

// Later: only this Text node re-emits SET_ATTRIBUTED_TEXT.
message.value = Markdown.parse("**done**")
```

### 4. Direct model / arbitrary attributes

Use this when you need attributes not covered by the builder helpers:

```kotlin
import dev.pathland.view.core.*

val rich = AttributedString.of(
    "Hi",
    runs = listOf(
        StyleRun(0, 2, listOf(TextAttribute.fontWeight(700f))),
        StyleRun(0, 2, listOf(TextAttribute.color(0xFF2563EB.toInt()))),
    ),
    links = listOf(LinkRun(1, 2, "https://pathland.dev")),
)
```

Here `StyleRun`/`LinkRun` ranges are **UTF-8 byte offsets**, matching the wire format.

### Supported attributes in v1

`FONT_SIZE`, `FONT_WEIGHT`, `COLOR`, `FONT_STYLE`, `FONT_DESIGN`, `UNDERLINE`, `STRIKETHROUGH`, plus link URLs.

Available builder helpers:

```kotlin
.bold(start, end)
.italic(start, end)
.monospaced(start, end)
.underline(start, end)
.strikethrough(start, end)
.fontSize(start, end, points)
.color(start, end, argb)
.link(start, end, url)
```

### Notes

- Node-level modifiers still apply as the base style; runs override their ranges:
  ```kotlin
  Text(rich).fontSize(17f).lineLimit(2)
  ```
- GTK, SSR HTML, and the DOM client render rich text; Qt currently falls back to the plain text.
- `Markdown.parse` only covers the inline subset: `**bold**`, `*italic*`, `` `code` ``, `~~strikethrough~~`, `[text](url)`, and backslash escapes.
Similar to Text in Swiftui, I want it to be build in.

content.text:
You’re right — native embedding is already the pattern (HTML renderer, ring interop), so reusing the shared Rust parser is the better call. My pure-Kotlin suggestion was only to avoid adding another native dependency to `pathland-view-core`; if we accept that (which the project already does), we keep **one parser** and avoid drift.

## Plan — make `Text(...)` parse inline Markdown automatically

### Decision

Use the existing shared Rust parser (`libpathland_markdown`) via JNA, and make it part of `pathland-view-core` so `Text(...)` is built-in. No second parser implementation.

To avoid the module cycle (`pathland-markdown` currently depends on view-core for `AttributedString`):

- Move the `dev.pathland.markdown.Markdown` JNA shim into `pathland-view-core`.
- Embed `libpathland_markdown` in the `pathland-view-core` jar (same pattern as `pathland-render-html`).
- Remove the separate `lib/java/pathland-markdown` Maven module (it is new/unreleased) and its reactor/CI/release wiring.
- Keep the Rust crates `pathland-markdown` + `pathland-markdown-capi` as the single parser implementation.

### Kotlin API

```kotlin
// Auto-parse inline Markdown (SwiftUI-like).
Text("Hello **world**")

// Literal text, no Markdown interpretation.
Text("**not bold**", markdown = false)

// Reactive string: parses whenever the signal changes.
Text(nameSignal)

// Reactive literal string.
Text(nameSignal, markdown = false)

// Pre-built rich text still works.
Text(attributedString)
Text(attributedSignal)
```

Signatures:

```kotlin
@JvmOverloads fun Text(text: String, markdown: Boolean = true): View
@JvmOverloads fun Text(text: Signal<String>, markdown: Boolean = true): View
fun Text(value: AttributedString): View
fun Text(value: Signal<AttributedString>): View
```

`@JvmOverloads` preserves existing Java-facing signatures.

### Markdown subset

Same inline subset as SwiftUI’s `Text` use case:

- `**bold**` → `FONT_WEIGHT` 700
- `*italic*` → `FONT_STYLE` Italic
- `` `monospaced` `` → `FONT_DESIGN` Monospaced
- `~~strikethrough~~` → `STRIKETHROUGH`
- `[label](url)` → link
- Backslash escapes and nesting

No headings, lists, block code, images, tables. Underscore emphasis (`_italic_`, `__bold__`) stays out unless we also extend the Rust parser; recommend keeping the current `*` forms for parity.

### Plain-text fast path

`Text("hello")` still parses, but when the result has no runs/links:

- emit the compact `SET_TEXT`, not the larger `SET_ATTRIBUTED_TEXT`
- use the simple renderer path
- keep the wire/arena overhead identical to today

Only rich results emit `SET_ATTRIBUTED_TEXT`. This applies to both static and reactive text, including transitions from plain → rich and rich → plain.

### Kotlin implementation

**Parser access**
- Move `Markdown.java` into `pathland-view-core` (`dev.pathland.markdown`).
- Add the native-jar embed step to `pathland-view-core/pom.xml`.
- Update `refresh-ide`, CI, and release staging to build/stage `libpathland_markdown` for view-core.
- Loader resolution stays: system property → embedded jar → local Rust debug build → `java.library.path`.

**Static `Text(String)`**
- Fast pre-scan for `*`, `~`, `` ` ``, `[`, `\`; if none, use plain `SET_TEXT` without touching JNA.
- Otherwise parse; if the result is plain, use plain text; if rich, use `attributedTextView`.

**Reactive `Text(Signal<String>)`**
- Wrap it in `Signals.computed { Markdown.parse(...) }` so parsing happens only when the string signal changes.
- Emitter chooses `SET_TEXT` vs `SET_ATTRIBUTED_TEXT` based on `AttributedString.isPlain`.
- Add `AttributedString.equals`/`hashCode` so computed equality suppression works.

**Caching / performance**
- Bounded parse cache keyed by string for static literals and repeated values.
- No native call for strings without Markdown markers.
- No reparse when the raw string is unchanged.
- Parser is O(n) on the inline text; plain text remains effectively free.

### Rust implementation

Make the Rust DSL match:

```rust
Text::new("Hello **world**")   // parses
Text::plain("**literal**")      // no parse
Text::with(|t| t.text_signal(sig))       // parses on change
Text::with(|t| t.plain_signal(sig))      // literal signal
```

- `pathland-engine` gains a `markdown_text` flag on `Node` (set by the text DSL).
- Static text: parse at build time in `pathland-view` (it already depends on `pathland-markdown`).
- Reactive text: the engine parses only when the raw string changes; unchanged text emits zero opcodes.
- If parsing yields no runs/links, keep the plain `SET_TEXT` path.
- `Text::plain` / `plain_signal` are the explicit opt-outs.

### Emitter / engine changes

- **Kotlin emitter**: attributed bindings may now carry plain values. Emit `SET_TEXT` for `isPlain`, `SET_ATTRIBUTED_TEXT` otherwise, in mount, reconcile, subtree, and signal effects.
- **Rust engine**: same rule for markdown text and markdown signal bindings; snapshot keeps the plain/rich mode so transitions emit the right opcode.
- Keep the existing `AttributedString` opcode/payload unchanged.

### Tests

- Kotlin:
  - `Text("**Hi**")` emits `SET_ATTRIBUTED_TEXT`.
  - `Text("Hi")` emits `SET_TEXT`.
  - `Text("**Hi**", markdown = false)` emits `SET_TEXT`.
  - Reactive plain → rich → plain emits the correct opcode sequence.
  - Parser parity with the Rust parser for the same inputs.
- Rust:
  - `Text::new` auto-parses; `Text::plain` does not.
  - Signals parse on change and emit zero opcodes when unchanged.
  - Steady-state zero allocation remains true for plain text.
- Update `spec/DSL.md`, `pathland-view-core/status.md`, `pathland-view/status.md`, `pathland-engine/status.md`, `pathland-markdown/status.md`, and the Java module docs.

### Follow-ups / gaps

- Underscore emphasis (`_`/`__`) if we want fuller SwiftUI parity.
- A benchmark proving the pre-scan/cache keep plain-text rendering at current cost.
- Remove the now-redundant `pathland-markdown` Java artifact and its native packaging after moving the shim into view-core.

Approve this and I’ll implement it. The main structural change is merging the JNA Markdown shim into `pathland-view-core` and removing the separate Java module, so `Text(...)` is genuinely built in.

    @Test
    fun reactiveTextParsesMarkdownAndFallsBackToPlain() {
        val label = signal("**Hi**")
        val sink = FrameOpcodeSink()
        val emitter = Emitter(sink)
        emitter.mount(Text(label), Environment.DEFAULT)
        assertTrue(sink.frame().opcodes().any { it.command() == Commands.Parameter.SET_ATTRIBUTED_TEXT })

        label.value = "plain"

        label.value = "__Bold__"
        val rich = sink.frame()
        assertEquals(1, rich.opcodes().size)
        assertEquals(Commands.Parameter.SET_ATTRIBUTED_TEXT, rich.opcodes().single().command())

content.text:
Done. `Text(...)` now parses inline Markdown automatically in both DSLs, with full underscore parity.

### Kotlin

```kotlin
Text("Hello **world**")          // auto-parses
Text("**literal**", markdown = false)
Text(signal)                    // parses on every signal change
Text(signal, markdown = false)  // literal reactive text
Text(attributedString)          // explicit rich text
```

Supported: `**bold**` / `__bold__`, `*italic*` / `_italic_`, `` `monospaced` ``, `~~strikethrough~~`, `[label](url)`, escapes, nesting. Intraword underscores stay literal (`snake_case`).

### Rust

```rust
Text::new("Hello **world**")   // auto-parses
Text::plain("**literal**")     // opt out
Text::with(|t| t.text_signal(sig))  // parses on change
Text::with(|t| t.plain_signal(sig)) // literal signal
```

### Implementation notes

- Reused the shared Rust parser via JNA; moved `dev.pathland.markdown.Markdown` into `pathland-view-core` and embedded `libpathland_markdown` in the view-core jar. Removed the separate `pathland-markdown` Java module.
- Added a cheap Markdown-marker pre-scan and a bounded parse cache. Plain results still emit compact `SET_TEXT`; only rich results emit `SET_ATTRIBUTED_TEXT`.
- Rust engine stores the raw Markdown source in the snapshot, so unchanged text emits zero opcodes; signal text is parsed only when it changes.
- Both renderers and the DOM client needed no changes.

### Verified

- `cargo test` — all Rust crates pass.
- `cargo run -p pathland-engine-golden -- --check` — current.
- `lib/rust/check-wasm.sh` — `no_std`/wasm32 preserved.
- TypeScript `typecheck` + `268` tests pass.
- Full Maven reactor `mvn test` passes, including the native Markdown shim and underscore parity test.

No commit was made.

# Deploying the Quarkus SSR demo

Runs the [Pathland Quarkus demo](pathland-quarkus-demo/) (server-side HTML at any
path + live `/ws` deltas) as a container — the application evidence for the Restack
proposal (issue #71, `docs/PREAPPLICATION-TODO.md`).

The image is multi-stage: it builds the Rust HTML renderer cdylib, embeds it into
the Java `pathland-render-html` jar (which the demo depends on), packages the
Quarkus app, and runs it on a JRE 17 runtime.

## Build

From the repository root (build context must be the root — the embed step needs
the Rust dylib and the Java reactor sources):

```bash
docker build -f lib/java/pathland-quarkus-demo/Dockerfile -t pathland-quarkus-demo .
```

The image's Maven step selects both `pathland-quarkus-demo` and
`pathland-quarkus-deployment`. The deployment module is not a Maven dependency of
the demo, but the runtime extension descriptor validates its dependencies against
it; omitting it makes a fresh (empty `~/.m2`) build fail Quarkus extension
verification.

## Run locally

```bash
docker run --rm -p 8080:8080 pathland-quarkus-demo
# → http://localhost:8080
```

A quick check that it serves:

```bash
curl -I http://localhost:8080/          # 200, text/html
curl http://localhost:8080/ | grep -o 'data-pathland-id'   # hydrated SSR markup
```

State defaults to the in-memory store (no Redis needed for the demo). To use
Redis, pass a `REDIS_URL` and the Redis `StateStore` in `pathland-server-core` is
selected at runtime — the standalone demo runs without it.

## Push to a registry

```bash
docker tag pathland-quarkus-demo ghcr.io/<org>/pathland-quarkus-demo:latest
docker push ghcr.io/<org>/pathland-quarkus-demo:latest
```

## Deploy to a host

Any platform that runs a Docker container exposing TCP 8080 works:

- **Railway / Fly.io** — point at the image (or use a Dockerfile deploy); set the
  public port to **8080**. The app binds `0.0.0.0` (see
  `application.properties`).
- **Hetzner / any VPS** — `docker run -d -p 8080:8080 --name pathland pathland-quarkus-demo`
  (optionally behind Caddy/nginx; forward `GET /` and the WebSocket `Upgrade`).
- **Platform port override** — the app honors `QUARKUS_HTTP_PORT` if a platform
  assigns a different port.

### Requirements

- **WebSocket support**: the demo keeps the first page live via `/ws` (raw-input
  events + `PLPL` deltas). The reverse proxy / load balancer must forward the
  WebSocket `Upgrade` headers; most PaaS do this by default.
- **Health check**: `GET /` returning 200 with HTML is the simplest probe. The
  container has no separate health endpoint.
- **Memory**: the JVM is capped at 256 MB (`-Xmx256m`); the demo is small.

# Releasing Pathland

Publishing a **GitHub Release** (tagged `vX.Y.Z`) runs
`.github/workflows/release.yml`, which sets the version from the tag, builds and
publishes every artifact, attaches the built files to the Release, and commits
the version back to `main`:

| Ecosystem | Artifacts | Registry |
|-----------|-----------|----------|
| Rust | `pathland-core`, `pathland-engine`, `pathland-view`, `pathland-core-transport`, `pathland-render-html` | crates.io |
| Java | `dev.pathland:*` libraries (incl. the renderer's native libs for windows-x86_64, linux-x86_64, linux-aarch64, macos-aarch64) | Maven Central |

## Versioning (tag-driven)

**The tag drives the version** — no pre-bump commit is needed:

- The workflow writes `X.Y.Z` (from the tag `vX.Y.Z`) into
  `lib/rust/Cargo.toml` (`[workspace.package] version` + the intra-workspace
  path-dep pins, via `cargo set-version --workspace`) and
  `lib/java/pom.xml` (via `mvn versions:set`) **in CI**, then publishes.
- A `bump` job then commits that version back to `main`, so `main` always
  reflects the latest release.

Tags must be `v<major>.<minor>.<patch>` (an optional pre-release suffix is
allowed); the `version` job fails on anything else. Releases are immutable per
version — pick a new tag to re-release.

## One-time setup

Repository secrets (Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions):

- `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN` — a crates.io API token with publish scope
  (https://crates.io/settings/tokens).
- `GPG_PRIVATE_KEY` — an armored GPG private key whose public key is on a
  keyserver (Central verifies the signatures).
- `GPG_PASSPHRASE` — that key's passphrase.
- `CENTRAL_USERNAME` / `CENTRAL_PASSWORD` — a Sonatype Central Portal **user
  token** (https://central.sonatype.com/account).

Also: `main` must be pushable by the workflow's `GITHUB_TOKEN` (the `bump` job).
If `main` is protected, allow the Actions bot, or the bump step fails (after a
successful publish).

## Release

1. Create a **GitHub Release** on `main` tagged `vX.Y.Z` (publish it).
2. The workflow runs:
   - `version` — derive + validate `X.Y.Z` from the tag.
   - `rust` — set the version, test the publishable crates, publish them to
     crates.io in dependency order, upload the `.crate` files.
   - `java-natives` — build `libpathland_render_html` for windows-x86_64,
     linux-x86_64, linux-aarch64, macos-aarch64.
    - `java` — set the version, stage the natives into the renderer jar, run
      `mvn -P release deploy` to Maven Central (auto-published after validation).
    - `bump` — commit the version back to `main`.
    - `release-assets` — attach the `.crate` files, the Java main jars, and the
      four native libs to the GitHub Release.

The Java deploy runs on **Maven 3.9.9** (pinned in the workflow): Maven 3.10
writes a `maven-metadata-local.xml` beside each artifact in the Central staging,
which the Portal rejects ("content that does NOT have a .pom file"). The demos
are **excluded from the release reactor** (`-pl '!pathland-demo-views-kotlin,!pathland-desktop-demo,!pathland-quarkus-demo,!pathland-spring-boot-demo'`)
— `central-publishing-maven-plugin` bundles every reactor module, ignoring
`maven.deploy.skip`, and the demos must not be published.

The publish steps are **idempotent**: a crate+version already on crates.io is
skipped, so re-running a partially failed release is safe (re-run the workflow
via `workflow_dispatch`, passing the `tag`). Maven Central rejects a re-deploy of
an existing version, so a Java re-run only helps if the Java deploy did not
complete.

## Local pre-flight

Rust — `cargo publish --dry-run -p pathland-core` validates the leaf crate (the
dependent crates can only be dry-run once their dependencies are on crates.io,
so the ordered CI publish validates them).

Java — `mvn -P release verify` builds and signs the sources/javadoc jars without
uploading. It needs GPG installed and a `central` server in `~/.m2/settings.xml`:

```xml
<server>
  <id>central</id>
  <username>TOKEN_USERNAME</username>
  <password>TOKEN_PASSWORD</password>
</server>
```

## Publishable crates (dependency order)

```
pathland-core → pathland-engine → pathland-view → pathland-core-transport → pathland-render-html
```

(`pathland-view-native`, `pathland-core-capi`, `pathland-render-gtk`,
`pathland-render-gtk-demo`, `pathland-html-golden`, `pathland-ts-codegen` are
**not** published — C-ABI cdylibs, the GTK renderer, and dev tools.)

## Published Java modules

`pathland-view-core` (Kotlin JVM engine/SPI + the sole authoring DSL),
`pathland-render-html`, `pathland-server-core` (runtime, telemetry adapters,
Redis state store, and the shared WS test harness), `pathland-spring-boot-starter`,
`pathland-quarkus`, `pathland-quarkus-deployment` (plus the `pathland-parent`
POM). The demo modules (`pathland-demo-views-kotlin`, `pathland-desktop-demo`,
`pathland-quarkus-demo`, `pathland-spring-boot-demo`) set `maven.deploy.skip`.

       lib/rust/target/debug/libpathland_markdown.so
  ```

- `docs/DEPLOY.md`: update the image description (“renderer + view-core embed Rust cdylibs”) and note the two build outputs.

### 3. Release workflow/docs
The new `pathland-markdown` crate is a dependency of `pathland-engine`/`pathland-view`, so it must be published to crates.io:
- `.github/workflows/release.yml`:
